content.rationale:
This is a code-to-code check: the dependent is the flat module src/verb_discard.rs and every prerequisite it leans on is code, so the gate is a runnable self-contained test crate. The crate pulls the module under test and the siblings it calls in through #[path] shims and drives verb_discard::run over scratch jj repositories made with jj git init, with real jj workspace add working copies and records written under .deccy/work/; the per-user draft-workspace root is a scratch HOME and the tests are serialized by that one shared HOME while each repository has its own canonical-path namespace.

It observes the decision's own observables rather than restating it: the record documents, jj workspace list, the working copies' change ids and commit ids, the directories under the per-user root, the node documents, the marker file, and the handler's returned lines. It covers the surface (one open draft per handle, a repeated handle naming one draft wherever the repeat falls in the call — a later repeat of an earlier handle is the same draft and is discarded once, so an adjacent-only dedupe is not enough — a call naming no handle and an unnamed argument refused at the argument surface before the store, --help from a root-less context answering with a line naming discard, and a reference a record carries — a node id, an edit id or its workspace name — read as a key that names no record); the whole-call refusal leaving every named record, workspace, directory and change untouched when any handle names no open record (unknown, landed, or a non-handle reference), and the refusal carrying every offending handle in the call among its evidence — each unknown handle and each landed handle when a call names several, and the non-handle reference when one is used as a handle — so no offender is dropped and the evidence is not limited to the first or the last one; the three acts on a normal draft (the working-copy change the workspace holds abandoned while the node's owning change keeps its commit, the jj workspace forgotten, the directory the handle derives removed); success silence; no marker, node or change written and other records retained byte for byte; a drifted open record discarded without refusal and without a substituted change; and the trunk-only refusal from a linked workspace naming the invocation workspace and discarding nothing. The non-adjacent repeat is observed with two real open drafts and the call [A, B, A]: both records leave, both workspaces are forgotten, both derived directories go, both working-copy changes are abandoned — bookmarked so a forgotten workspace cannot hide a skipped abandonment — the node's owning change and the invocation's change are untouched, no node is written, and the call succeeds with no lines; an implementation that removes only neighbouring duplicates keeps the third occurrence, processes A, then B, then A again, and refuses on A's already-removed record after A's and B's records have left — a partial commit presented as a refusal — and the check rejects it.

The commit boundary is observed through induced failures and separating cases. The registry removal is the commit for the whole call and not for one draft: with two drafts, the second draft's derived path is a regular file after its workspace is forgotten and its directory cleared, so its directory removal fails with not-a-directory after the first draft's change, workspace and directory acts have completed; the call refuses, both records stay at their handles, and the first draft's completed acts stand with no rollback. The two-draft case assumes the handles are processed in argument order, so the draft recorded first is the one whose acts complete first. The removal's subject is the handle derivation — the per-user root, the repository's namespace and the handle — and not the path the record stores: a record's workspace.path is rewritten to a decoy directory carrying a file, and the derived directory leaves while the decoy and its file survive and the record is removed. Only that directory is removed: with two open drafts in one namespace, discarding one leaves the sibling's record, derived directory, workspace and change, the namespace directory above the handle, and the per-user root in place, and discarding the sibling afterwards still leaves the namespace and the root in place when no record names a directory in them. Directory absence is not workspace absence: with a real open draft whose derived directory is removed while jj still lists its workspace, and whose working-copy change a bookmark keeps visible so a forgotten workspace cannot hide it, the workspace's change is abandoned before the forget; a handler that skips the change act whenever the derived path is absent leaves that visible change and fails the check, and only a name jj no longer lists skips the act. The per-user root's literal location and the namespace's spelling are not fixed by the prerequisites, so the fixtures place and observe the derived directory using the root and namespace the landing seams use (a scratch HOME, the namespace the repository's canonical path gives and the handle); the check never reads the removal's subject from the record's stored path, and the exact jj invocation behind the forget and the abandonment stays the seams'.

A failure before the commit refuses, and the check induces the failures the decision names. The abandonment is a crossing of its own: with a PATH whose first entry holds a jj wrapper that delegates every crossing to the real jj except abandon, which exits 1 with a distinctive stderr, a discard of one open draft refuses, the refusal carries the failed crossing's evidence, and the record, the workspace, the derived directory and the change the workspace holds stand — a handler that dropped the abandonment's status would go on to forget the workspace, remove the directory and remove the record, and the check would see a success. The workspace crossing is induced the same way: a wrapper that delegates every crossing except workspace forget, which exits 1 with a distinctive stderr, makes the discard refuse, and the record, the workspace and the derived directory the failed forget would have reached stand. The read that identifies the change the workspace holds is induced too: a wrapper that fails only the log of the workspace's own revision while jj still lists the workspace makes the discard refuse rather than skip the change act and go on to forget the workspace, remove the directory and remove the record — so a failing read is a failure before the commit, and only a workspace jj no longer lists, the jj workspace list not naming it, is the gone workspace the decision carries through as no abandonment. An absent derived directory does not make a listed workspace gone: the abandonment is the crossing of the workspace, read from jj's enumeration, not of the directory, so a listed workspace whose directory has been removed still has its change abandoned. The draft's change act precedes the forget, so the forget check asserts the no-record-removal boundary and not that the change survives; the abandon and read checks refuse before any act and assert that everything stands.
